execution.implementation: dated PubMed and PMC evidence, deterministic local orthogonal-assay map, and a genuine Rosalind task-chooser observation

observations: The recorded PubMed searches retained one BLI kinetics protocol and three records matching nanobody, surface plasmon resonance, and ELISA title-or-abstract terms.
Three selected application records resolved to PMC open-access records; the selected BLI protocol had no PMC record on the retrieval date.
Rosalind Workbench returned its ready task chooser for the recorded case-specific invocation.
interpretation: The record set supports teaching an orthogonal strategy that combines label-free kinetics with plate-based binding or specificity measurements without comparing cross-paper numerical values.
limitations: PubMed query-term matches do not verify protocol quality.
The selected papers use different targets and experimental systems.
PMC access status is time-sensitive and bibliographic discoverability does not imply open full text.
The Rosalind call opened only the task chooser and did not execute a scientific job.

sources: NCBI Entrez E-Utilities PubMed ESearch, ESummary, and EFetch
provenance.note: The literature APIs supplied bibliographic, query-match, and PMC observations; the local script produced the deterministic assay map; the separate Rosalind observation preserves the exact task-chooser response and states that no scientific job ran.

reproduction: Repeat both retained PubMed searches and compare the returned PMID slices with outputs/query-verification.json.
Repeat identifier-specific PMC lookups before making current access or license statements.
Run python scripts/summarize.py from the case directory and compare outputs/results.json.
Inspect the preview against the retained assay-evidence map.
Compare any new Rosalind launcher response with outputs/rosalind-open-observation.json without treating it as assay evidence.
